questions.q: What four real states carry northfield-pipeline-orchestrator's main path?
options: CrawlRawZone, RunETLJob, LoadRedshift, and NotifySuccess (with a NotifyFailure catch path)
Only a single Lambda function that does everything
CrawlRawZone, LoadRedshift, RunETLJob, NotifyFailure, in that order
IngestS3, CrawlRawZone, RunETLJob, LoadRedshift, QueryAthena
questions.explain: The chain is crawl the raw zone, run the ETL job, load Redshift, then notify success — with any failure caught and routed to NotifyFailure.

questions.q: Why does RunETLJob use glue:startJobRun.sync instead of the plain glue:startJobRun action?
options: The .sync integration makes Step Functions wait for the Glue job to actually finish before moving to the next state
It's required syntax with no functional difference
It runs the job twice for redundancy
.sync makes the job run faster
questions.explain: The .sync suffix is a synchronous service integration — Step Functions waits for completion instead of firing and moving on immediately.

questions.q: What does every task state's Catch clause do?
options: Routes any error in that state straight to the NotifyFailure state, ensuring a human is told when something breaks
Automatically retries the failed state up to 100 times
Silently ignores the error and continues to the next state
Deletes the partial output from that state
questions.explain: Every task state's Catch routes States.ALL errors to NotifyFailure, which publishes to SNS so failures are surfaced, not swallowed.

questions.q: What triggers northfield-pipeline-orchestrator to run each night, and when?
options: An EventBridge rule (northfield-nightly-trigger) on a cron schedule at 6:00 AM UTC
A human manually starting it from the console every morning
S3 event notifications the moment any file is uploaded
It runs continuously with no schedule
questions.explain: northfield-nightly-trigger uses cron(0 6 * * ? *) to fire the state machine at 6 AM UTC, after the overnight SQL Server export finishes.

questions.q: What happens if the SQL Server export is running late and hasn't finished when the 6 AM trigger fires?
options: The crawler still runs but finds no new partition, and the ETL job's bookmark means nothing new gets reprocessed — an uneventful run, not a broken one
The entire state machine immediately fails and pages an on-call engineer
Step Functions deletes the previous night's data to avoid conflicts
The pipeline silently loads stale data into Redshift without any indication
questions.explain: A late export just means no new partition is found; the crawler and bookmarked ETL job handle that gracefully rather than erroring or loading stale/incomplete data.
